headline: Valve lets you build your own Steam Machine with SteamOS
summary: Valve is making SteamOS available for custom PC builds, allowing users to install the operating system on their own hardware.
details: Valve has officially announced that users can now build their own Steam Machine using custom PC parts. This is made possible with the latest SteamOS 3.8.10 release, which includes significant improvements for compatibility with both Intel and AMD platforms.

While it was technically possible to install SteamOS on custom hardware before, compatibility was largely limited to AMD systems and the process was complex, often requiring a Steam Deck recovery image. The new updates aim to simplify this for a wider range of hardware.

Valve is also working closely with Nvidia to ensure future support for their graphics cards in SteamOS. While Nvidia support may not arrive this year, a dedicated team is actively developing the necessary drivers.

For those looking for a console-like PC experience, SteamOS can offer a good experience on setups similar to a Steam Machine, especially when connected to a TV. However, features like HDMI-CEC support are still pending.

The current SteamOS installer is designed for fresh installations and does not yet support dual-booting alongside other operating systems. Valve envisions a future where installing SteamOS on a desktop alongside another OS will be a more seamless experience.

headline: SpaceX inks $6.3B AI compute deal with open-source lab Reflection AI
summary: Reflection AI will pay $150 million monthly for access to Nvidia's latest AI chips and hardware at SpaceX's Tennessee data center, starting July 2026.
details: Open-source AI startup Reflection AI has secured a significant compute deal with SpaceX, agreeing to pay $150 million per month from July 2026 through 2029. The contract, potentially worth up to $6.3 billion, grants Reflection access to Nvidia's latest GB300 AI chips and supporting hardware at SpaceX's Colossus 2 data center in Tennessee.

This deal marks Reflection AI's first major compute commitment and underscores the growing importance of open-weight AI models. The startup, founded by former Google DeepMind researchers, positions itself as an open-source alternative to closed frontier labs like OpenAI and Anthropic.

The agreement comes amid increasing attention on open-source AI, particularly following U.S. government actions against closed models. Reflection AI stated that the deal highlights the strategic importance of open source in the AI ecosystem and provides them with the necessary resources to build advanced open models at scale.

SpaceX's Colossus data center was initially built for Elon Musk's xAI. As xAI's internal projects have shifted, SpaceX has begun leasing its substantial AI chip capacity to leading AI laboratories, leveraging its infrastructure to generate revenue.

While smaller than SpaceX's deals with Anthropic ($1.25B/month) and Google ($920M/month), the Reflection AI contract demonstrates SpaceX's strategy of monetizing its AI hardware. Both parties have the option to terminate the contract with 90 days' notice after the initial three months.
